01-colour-density: Keep as an optional restrained control. The dessert gains modest colour weight while the plate and visible skin remain plausible. Suggested range 0.5–0.75; the supplied example uses 0.75.
02-blue-density: Useful and scene dependent. The warm-masonry architecture example shows richer blue sky clearly. The dark lake benefits less from additional density: prefer about 0.35–0.5 there; architecture can support 0.5–0.7.
03-highlight-gamut: Negative result on the clipped portrait JPEG: strength 0.7 makes the white sky a flat pale grey without recovering detail. Keep this evidence; recommend Off for that scene. Use only restrained output shaping on highlights with surviving detail, and prefer the RAW approach in folder 08.
04-skin-and-tone-colour: Subtle alternative rendering. Skin stays plausible in the outdoor and indoor portraits, with a small change in surrounding colour separation. Suggested range 0.4–0.6; preference can reasonably go either way.
05-complete-recipes: A coordinated RAW recipe changes the starting rendering, warmth and highlights together. The additional WB-only comparisons isolate the relative scene-linear colour balance. These are choices of finish; the common RAW baseline makes their effects assessable without comparing different decoders.
06-texture: A small texture change, not restored detail. Inspect the 100% crops: fine texture remains, and the inspected examples show no strong edge halos. Conservative portrait strength 0–0.4 is more convincing than a universal softening/sharpening default.
07-iso-grain-monochrome: Grain is an optional rougher finish; it does not improve resolved detail. Prefer 0.2–0.4 on the dim portrait. The high-ISO fixed-versus-adaptive comparison isolates reduced added grain at ISO 5000. Monochrome has its own grayscale baseline so colour conversion cannot hide the tone/texture change.
08-highlight-protection-raw: The strongest highlight result. Roof panel variations survive the protected rendering where the hard-clipped baseline is flat white. Suggested strength 0.6–0.8. This uses real DNG output headroom, not a new sensor exposure or recovery of sensor-clipped data.
09-true-3d-lut: A restrained alternative look, with reusable 17-cube and 33-cube files. The 33-cube follows the direct colour target more closely. The extra LUT is not itself a guarantee of a better photograph; inspect the target and representation comparisons in folder 10.
10-validation-fidelity: This folder measures approximation error. BEFORE is the direct authored target; AFTER is a native matrix/curve software approximation or sampled 17/33-cube. Native fitting is close for many natural colours but has larger errors at some gamut boundaries and near black. No Fujifilm reference calibration is claimed.
11-combinations: Use scene-specific combinations rather than stacking every effect at the same strength. The portrait keeps modest colour and texture; landscape and dessert omit added grain; the dim portrait omits extra colour/blue density. Individual folders remain available to judge each contribution. No universal quality win is claimed.
